subject: how to calculate MPA and VPA in different bout length

messages.author: 98fb57d9ed19af69
messages.subject: how to calculate MPA and VPA in different bout length
parts:
Dear Vincent
I am writing to inquire about the calculation of moderate and vigorous physical activity (MPA and VPA) in different bout lengths. I have found that I am able to derive moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) in different bout lengths, but not MPA and VPA. Furthermore, the value of unbouted and total MPA and VPA are not equal, which has led me to wonder whether there is a specific parameter I need to apply to obtain accurate MPA and VPA values with different bout durations.

Would you be able to provide me with guidance on how to calculate MPA and VPA using different bout lengths? Are there any specific parameters or adjustments I need to make to ensure accuracy in my calculations?

Thank you in advance for your assistance. I look forward to hearing from you soon.

Best regards,

Puchen Zhou

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: how to calculate MPA and VPA in different bout length
parts:
Dear Puchen Zhou,

Bout calculation for MPA and VPA separately are not available in GGIR for now. The only solution I can think of with the current GGIR version would be to trick the definition of the thresholds arguments so that you include two different thresholds for moderate physical activity (your moderate and your vigorous thresholds). You then would get two datasets for the part 5 in the results folder, one for each combination of thresholds. And you could use the MVPA information from the two datasets to derive the specific MPA and VPA thresholds. Not sure if this would work well as I have never tried this before.

Best,
Jairo

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: how to calculate MPA and VPA in different bout length
parts:
Hi Jairo and Puchen,

If you set the mvpa threshold at a level that is indicative of vigorous activity then your MVPA bouts estimates will reflect vigorous activity bouts. If you additionally set the light activity threshold at moderate level, your LIPA bouts will reflect MPA bouts. The main challenge for you is to be aware of this new interpretation of the variable names.

However, this comes at the cost of LIPA being merged with inactivity.
To address that you could run GGIR separately with normal thresholds to extract the relative contribution of LIPA and inactivity and translate those to the analyses above. 

My proposal would be to first prove the scientific relevance of capturing all these bout  types via the approach I have described above before we consider adding this to GGIR.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
